claims.claim: Exact stationary rarity. For 0<p<1, put α=1-p. If π is the stationary law, then the complete-state probability is Π_{n,p}:=π([n])=∏_{r=1}^n [rα^r/(n-(n-r)α^r)]. Equivalently, R_{n,p}:=Π_{n,p}^{-1}=∏_{r=1}^n [1+(n/r)(α^{-r}-1)].
claims.evidence: For 0<p<1 the finite subset chain is irreducible, so its stationary law is unique and permutation invariant. For a fixed r-set A, stationarity and the transition rule give M_r=α^r[M_r+(r/n)(M_{r-1}-M_r)]: after acquisition, A is present precisely when it was already present or exactly one member was missing and that member was drawn, and then every member survives. Hence M_r/M_{r-1}=rα^r/[n-(n-r)α^r]. Multiplication from M_0=1 gives M_n=π([n]); taking factorwise reciprocals gives the stated R product. Exact rational reconstruction independently matched every inclusion moment and both products in all 72 tested instances.
claims.search_method: Direct stationary inclusion-moment derivation, followed by exact-rational reconstruction for n=1,...,12 and six rational loss probabilities.

claims.claim: Finite-n hitting-time sandwich. Let H_n=∑_{j=1}^n 1/j and A_{n,p}:=(R_{n,p}-1)/(1-α^n). Then for every n and 0<p<1, A_{n,p}≤E[T_{n,p}]≤H_n A_{n,p}.
claims.evidence: Let h_k be the mean hitting time from size k and e_k=h_k-h_{k+1}. Upward skip-freeness identifies e_k with the passage time k→k+1. The nested adjacent-state coupling gives e_k≤e_{k+1}. First-step analysis yields u_ke_k=1+Σ_{r<k}e_rF_k(r), with u_k=(n-k)α^{k+1}/n. The same coupling gives the required pointwise tail-sum domination; Abel summation with e_r-e_{r-1}≥0 therefore makes the recurrence numerator nondecreasing. Consequently (n-k)e_k is nondecreasing and h_0≤H_ne_{n-1}. Kac's return identity gives R-1=Σ_{k<n}P_n(K_1=k)h_k, while P_n(K_1<n)=1-α^n. Thus A is a conditional convex average of h_0,...,h_{n-1}, so e_{n-1}≤A≤h_0≤H_ne_{n-1}≤H_nA. The checker verified all recurrences, monotonicities, Kac's identity, and both inequalities exactly.
claims.search_method: Independent passage-time and Kac-identity proof; exhaustive one-step coupling check through n=8 and exact-rational chain solutions through n=12.

claims.claim: Asymptotic closure throughout the non-classical range. For every fixed η>0, uniformly over η(log n)/n²≤p_n<1, E[T_{n,p_n}]=(1+o(1))A_{n,p_n}=(1+o(1))(R_{n,p_n}-1)/(1-(1-p_n)^n).
claims.evidence: The exact passage recurrence implies e_k/e_{k-1}≥k(1-α^k)/[(n-k)α^{k+1}]. With m=⌊n/2⌋ and β=m(1-α^m), the assumed lower bound on p gives β≥c_η log n uniformly: use 1-(1-p)^m≥mp/2 when mp≤1, and ≥1-e^{-1} otherwise. For a_j=e_{n-j}/e_{n-1} and J=⌊β/2⌋, inversion of the ratio bound gives a_{j+1}≤(j/β)a_j for j<J. Hence Σ_{j=2}^J a_j=O(β^{-1}) and a_J≤β^{-1}2^{-J+2}. Monotonicity of (n-k)e_k gives a_j≤Ja_J/j for j≥J, whose harmonic tail is o(1) uniformly because β≥c_η log n. Therefore h_0/e_{n-1}=1+o(1) uniformly. Since e_{n-1}≤A≤h_0, the asserted equivalence follows.
claims.search_method: Uniform quantifier audit at both p→0 and p→1, analytic domination of all passage levels, and exact-rational verification of the finite recurrence and ratio inequality.

claims.claim: The resulting regimes differ from the product-of-marginals prediction. (i) If p=γ(log n)/n² with fixed γ>0, then E[T_{n,p}]∼n^{γ+1}/(γ log n). (ii) If (log n)/n²≪p≪1/n, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼n²p. (iii) If p=c/n with fixed c>0, then n^{-1}log E[T_{n,p}]→I(c):=∫_0^1 log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x)dx>log(1+c). (iv) If np→∞, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼(n²/2)log(1/(1-p)).
claims.evidence: Writing L=log R, for p=o(1/n) the uniform factor expansion gives L=n²p+O(n³p²). At p=γlog n/n² this yields R∼n^γ and 1-α^n∼γlog n/n, proving (i); in regime (ii), the error is o(n²p), R→∞, and |log(np)|=o(n²p), proving the logarithmic equivalent. For p=c/n, the summands form a uniformly controlled Riemann array converging to the stated continuous integrand. Since e^{cx}-1>cx for x>0, its integral is strictly greater than log(1+c). Finally, with ℓ=-log α, exact factorization gives L=n(n+1)ℓ/2+nlog n-log(n!)+Σ_r log(1-(1-r/n)e^{-rℓ}). The last sum has absolute value at most Σ_{r≥1}-log(1-e^{-rℓ})≤π²/(6ℓ). When np→∞, nℓ→∞, so both this correction and the O(n) factorial term are o(n²ℓ), while 1-α^n→1. Claim 2 then transfers all four estimates to E[T]. The checker independently verified the exact pre-log factorization.
claims.search_method: Separate analytic derivation for all four asymptotic regimes, including endpoint-uniform error estimates and exact-rational verification of the product factorization.

target_evidence: The exact target asks to close the lower/upper asymptotic gap in the non-classical regimes, with tightness of the conjectured lower/mean-field scale stated only as the ideal outcome. Claim 2 instead proves a uniform asymptotic equivalent at an explicit exact-product scale for every fixed η>0 and ηlog n/n²≤p<1. This covers the source's fixed-multiple super-classical regime and every larger non-classical regime, including the intermediate, c/n, and np→∞ cases; Claim 3 supplies their explicit scales. Proving that the preferred mean-field prediction is false, while determining the actual tight scale throughout the requested range, still fully resolves the target. Accordingly, the draft's FULL claimed resolution is ACCURATE rather than overstated.
